subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and what public config shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix would add public config surface and intentionally let high-risk tools pass through a requester that cannot call them directly.

options.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
options.body: Add a documented selfDeny or delegateOnly-style field with deny precedence, /tools visibility, ACP behavior, and tests for requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader per-spawn tool restriction design also covers requester self-denial and naming consistency.

options.title: Reject new config surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or prompt-level delegation as the supported pattern, accepting that config-level separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add a documented selfDeny or delegateOnly-style field with deny precedence, /tools visibility, ACP behavior, and tests for requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available current-main routing signal for this tool-policy/config/security boundary is Peter Steinberger's recent ownership of the central files.
